title: Still Life with Flowers, a Silver-gilt Goblet, Dried Fruit, Sweetmeats, Bread Sticks, Wine and a Pewter Pitcher
source: Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid, P001620 (public domain). Full resolution from Wikimedia Commons: Clara Peeters - Mesa (Prado) 01.jpg (3051 x 2162 px)
caption: A feast from 1611, and the painter is hiding somewhere on the table. Can you find her before the zoom? #womeninart #stilllife #clarapeeters #oilpainting #hiddendetails
_verify: VERIFIED, Museo del Prado (museodelprado.es/en/the-collection/art-work/still-life-with-flowers-a-silver-gilt-goblet/97a18fea-112a-417a-9a8a-6665a44cc331): THIS painting, P001620, 1611, 52 x 73 cm; 'Clara Peeters painted her self-portrait three times on the gilt goblet and four times on the pewter jug'; the many signatures and reflected self-portraits are 'a form of assertion, perhaps because she was a woman in a profession dominated by men'; they heighten the illusion that we see her as she paints; the half-eaten pretzel suggests someone has been at the table; reflections were a recognized artistic challenge she eagerly took up; signed and dated 'CLARA . P . Ao . 1611 .' lower left of the front.

VERIFIED, The Art Newspaper, 25 Oct 2016 (theartnewspaper.com/2016/10/25/it-only-took-200-years-prado-stages-its-first-show-dedicated-to-a-female-artist): in this Prado 1611 still life she appears 'in a headdress and ruff reflected in the flagon'; a 1612 Karlsruhe still life shows her holding brushes and palette (different painting, not used); one of the few women working as professional painters in 17th-century Europe; 39 attributed works; 'The Art of Clara Peeters' was the Prado's first exhibition dedicated to a female artist in its 200-year history (2016-2017).

VERIFIED, NPR, 30 Nov 2016 (npr.org/sections/parallels/2016/11/30/503129505): little is known about her; birth and death dates unclear; barely 40 paintings survive; curator Alejandro Vergara mentions 'seven reflections with her face'. Prado gives her dates as Antwerp (?) 1588 - Antwerp (?) 1621, other sources differ (1594-c.1640; c.1587-after 1636).
NOT CLAIMED: that it was painted in Antwerp (likely, unverified for this panel), or that the bouquet mixes seasons.

FOCUS WARNING: the reflections are tiny. At 3051 px the goblet cup is roughly 300-400 px wide and each face is likely only ~10-25 px; the slide 6/7 boxes can show the goblet and the jug, but the faces themselves will be barely legible. Signature box (slide 8) is a guess: lower left of the table front; re-tune on the real image.

slides.headline: Someone is hiding in this painting. Find her.
slides.sub: Clara Peeters, Still Life with Flowers and a Gilt Goblet, 1611

slides.headline: A feast in 1611
slides.text: 1611: a feast on a table, flowers, gold, sweets and wine. The painter, Clara Peeters, was one of very few professional women painters.

slides.headline: Who was Clara?
slides.text: Yet we know almost nothing about her: not when she was born, not when she died. Only about forty paintings survive. But she left clues.

slides.headline: Someone was just here
slides.text: Look at the pretzels: one is half eaten. Someone was sitting at this table a moment ago. Who? Keep looking.

slides.headline: Everything shines
slides.text: Every surface is polished: the wine glass, the pewter, the gold. Painting reflections was a test of skill, and she took it on eagerly.

slides.headline: Look at the goblet
slides.text: Now zoom into the gilded goblet. On its round bumps, tiny faces appear: three reflections of Clara herself, as if painting this very picture.

slides.headline: Four more
slides.text: And there's more. In the pewter jug she appears four more times, in a headdress and ruff. Seven self-portraits on one table.

slides.headline: Signed, CLARA P.
slides.text: Why hide there? Perhaps to assert herself: she also signed it, CLARA P. 1611. A woman in a men's profession, refusing to vanish.

slides.headline: Did you find her?
slides.text: In 2016 she became the first woman with her own exhibition at the Prado, after almost 200 years. Did you spot her before the zoom?
